statement: A factory makes bolts that are designed to be $40$ millimeters long. A bolt is exactly at the limit of the allowed error when its length $L$, in millimeters, satisfies $|L - 40| = 0.6$. Which lengths satisfy this equation?

choices.misconception: I solved only $L - 40 = 0.6$ and forgot that the expression inside the absolute value can also equal $-0.6$.
I wrote the second case as $-L - 40 = 0.6$, putting the minus sign only on $L$, and got $L = -40.6$.
I gave the two values of $L - 40$ instead of solving for $L$.

hints: The absolute value of a number is $0.6$ when the number is $0.6$ or $-0.6$.

solutions.reliable: $|L - 40| = 0.6$ means $L - 40 = 0.6$ or $L - 40 = -0.6$. So $L = 40.6$ or $L = 39.4$. Both are exactly $0.6$ millimeters from the design length of $40$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
